newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain grains prices expected to rise in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Spain grains prices expected to rise in 1997.

text.p: Spanish cereal prices are expected to soar in coming months as a lack of rain is seen cutting harvest, traders said on Monday.
Recent rainfall raised hopes of softer prices but in fact left the market little changed, amid no relief coming from foreign market prices either, traders in Spain said.
"We'll end the year with prices higher than now," a Madrid-based dealer said.

"Rain after all was very limited. The only prices which are really falling are foreign ones. A drought in Spain is very tough, more dangerous than in the Northern countries because we've got the hottest weather," he added.
Today Spain's ex-farm milling wheat was trading at around 28,000 pesetas per tonne, unchanged since April 18, while imported milling wheat slid to around 26,000 from 27,000.
"Rain didn't change prospects that much," a trader in Barcelona said, "and what is playing against us is also the fact that foreign prices have been sustained".
Some farmers have been hoarding crop stores in anticipation of higher prices.
"Farmers are saying for example that barley is trading at around 24,000 per tonne, but it's really hard to find somebody who really wants to sell barley at that price," a dealer added.
Estimations of the 1997 harvest vary from predicting a 15 to a 30 percent fall versus last year's crop of around 20 million tonnes.
Dealers added that the lack of rain was hurting southern regions most, where hard wheat is mainly produced and soft wheat is limited.
The only exception was thought to be maize, with the crop seen increasing slightly this year and prices expected to ease a bit as a consequence.
